Legislation_Text: For Utah nursing homes, state legislation requires: (b) The facility shall employ a RN for at least eight consecutive hours a day, seven days a week. (c) The facility shall designate a RN to serve as the DON on a full-time basis. A person may not concurrently serve as the DON and as a charge nurse. A skilled level of care facility must provide 24-hour licensed nursing services. (a) The facility shall ensure that nursing staff are present on the premises at all times to meet the needs of residents. A licensed nurse shall serve as charge nurse on each shift.

West Virginia requires at least 2.25 HPRD total nursing personnel (RNs, LPNs, CNAs) per resident per day statewide (WVC Title 64, §8.14). An RN must be on duty 8 consecutive hours every day; in facilities with fewer than 60 beds the DON may satisfy this. The DON must be an RN on duty full-time at least 5 days per week, 8 hours per day on day shift. Licensed nurse and nurse aide time may be combined so long as total meets the 2.25 HPRD minimum; a licensed nurse must serve as charge nurse on each shift.
